semantic_contract.canonical_authority: UnifiedDB typed semantic state + append/replay commitments
semantic_contract.lineage_identity: canonical root chain + selected lineage + external rollback floor

architectures.layout: independent canonical/graph/index stores with explicit coordination
one typed ClayCode query/transaction API over specialized physical stores
risks: coordination remains external to one engine

architectures.layout: UnifiedDB canonical commit + durable projection outbox; ClayGraph/FTS/vector replay asynchronously
architectures.historical_mechanism_evidence: U2: 1200 constructed trials, 0 final mismatch after replay vs 533 torn unsynchronized; outbox write p50 slower than monolith

architectures.layout: file-backed UnifiedDB main + ClayGraph ATTACH, rollback journal DELETE/FULL, one bounded cross-file transaction for semantic head + projection admission/batch
strengths: SQLite cross-file atomicity contract outside WAL
architectures.local_proxy: rollback across both files observed; separate parallel run measured attached p50 ~1.48x two separate commits

architectures.layout: verified fixed private SQLite + WAL for canonical store; ClayGraph remains async/rebuildable with StateProjectionCertificate
risks: ATTACH is not crash-atomic across files in WAL
architectures.promotion_role: candidate pending exact target private-SQLite gate

architectures.layout: canonical semantic state + graph/index structures physically consolidated into one engine/file where feasible
strengths: lowest coordination surface in some workloads
risks: derived data gains accidental operational coupling
architectures.historical_mechanism_evidence: U2 in-process mixed-read monolith did not materially beat same-process logical separate stores; monolith had lower write-path cost than outbox in the synthetic mechanism test

decision_law: correctness/replay/provenance/selection/recovery first; among passing architectures choose physical lowering by target p50/p95/p99, concurrency, write amplification, fsync/io, RSS/CPU, projection lag and rebuild time
